input.query: update user PATCH users controller service

content.text: Repositories have elided parts; read them and the rest of service.

candidates.explanation: The merge order is reversed: `{ ...payload, ...UserMapper.toDomain(entity) }`. The existing DB entity is spread last, so its values override every field in the payload (firstName, lastName, role, and so on). The save then writes the old values back, and the endpoint returns 200 with the unchanged user. The document repository does this correctly, with the existing user first and the payload second.

fix.description: Spread the existing entity first and the payload last, so the payload overrides the stored values: `UserMapper.toPersistence({ ...UserMapper.toDomain(entity), ...payload })`. UsersService.update passes undefined for fields that were not supplied, and those would overwrite existing values. To avoid that, strip undefined keys from the payload before merging.
